Remove request sent. Check the Photos face on your watch, then restore the plugin and reconnect in the companion app.

• Sending makes the Photos face the current one. • The watch’s answer goes to the stock plugin, so this app can only say the request was sent. • Galaxy Wearable may not list photos sent from here, and saving its Photos screen may replace them. • Every send carries the clock, since the watch draws none without one: the one chosen, else the one last sent, else the face’s own. Its choices come from the watch plugin on this phone. Choose No clock on Styles to send the face without one. • The Photos face has to be in the watch’s face list. It comes with the watch, but it can be removed there.

The Photos face’s styles, as the watch plugin on this phone pictures them: where the clock sits. Each is drawn in the clock’s colour, which is on Canvas. The style belongs to the whole face, whichever photo is shown, and goes with every send. No clock sends the face without its clock settings, and the watch then draws none.
The colours the watch offers its clock. The colour belongs to the whole face, whichever photo is shown, and goes with every send; the one last sent stays until you choose another.
The face is set to have no clock: sends leave the clock out, and the watch then draws none. Choose a style on Styles to bring it back.

The watch plugin on this phone doesn’t list the clock’s choices, so they can’t be changed here. Every send still carries a clock, since the watch draws none without one: the one last sent, or the face’s own, style 1 in white.
